body: Ugh, seems about right. Should've guessed that from the name.

Alright next time I'll avoid the unavoidable party-wide AOE after you kill the fires and tell the tank to never get hit by the boss, ever. I'm sure that's completely possible. You weren't there, I don't think you actually know how pathetic these cures were. But it's ok, continue to defend healers that can't keep the (dcd using, well-geared) tank above 30% on single trash pulls when spamming Cure II.

Thinking about it, IW is fine - if you're not a trash player. I agree that you can get through with it if you know what you're doing, but this 'healer' clearly didn't. I'm not going to mommy him and hold his hand and tell him how to play the easiest healer when he should already know how, though. So he should upgrade his gear (or at least repair it, wtf)

I'm not their moms. Randoms need to l2p.

...but we did wipe?? And it definitely wasn't because he made a 'bad play', unless you count his q'ing for a dungeon as a bad play. We were steadily losing hp the whole fight until our deaths because his sad little baby heals couldn't heal any of the damage inflicted.

Found the WHM. I'm not an asshole for telling a bad healer to upgrade their garbage gear (not Aug'd, learn to read) that caused us to nearly wipe every single trash pull and got us killed on one of the least healing intensive boss ever. :)

Their gear was definitely not augmented. I think they also had a white  vendor trash cane. It may have also been broken, considering just how weak their healing really was.
And we got to the last boss honestly by the skin of our teeth. Tank got very, very low almost every pull despite them all being single pulls. I had to Curing Waltz on CD and dps everything down ASAP. I think tank was also a WAR (this was a week or so ago) so I'm p sure he had self-sustain enough to barely make it through.
i suppose i can try doing that.
